item.title: [infoq] Snowflake CoCo AI 成本优化指南：7 个关键方法 | 技术实践
item.description: Snowflake CoCo turns natural language into real workflows, running SQL and multi-step processes with LLM calls, but consumes credits per token and can easily blow budgets. This article walks through seven governance levers, starting with usage history views in SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE to track per-user credit consumption, then default-behavior optimization and strict constraints. It's practical guidance for teams using CoCo for agentic apps who need cost control.

The latest release is Apple macOS-certified, so no manual security overrides are needed, and it adds skills management, terminal/git integration, file preview, @file/{skill_name} skill invocation, plus beta Telegram and mobile LAN sync. Pi users who prefer a local GUI for agent work may want to try it.

item.description: Doubao's upgraded video calling lets the AI ingest audio, video, and text simultaneously, speak when appropriate, and reduces awkward conversational pauses by about 50% versus classic cascaded systems, according to official evaluation. Underneath, Volcano Engine's MMT (multimodal transport system) replaces traditional RTC: it uses QUIC and MoQ for a unified session, cutting connection time from seconds to hundreds of milliseconds and preventing out-of-sync audio/model states. item.title: [v2ex] [AI SaaS 产品推荐] KIE Alternatives in 2026: Seedance and MiniMax H3 Priced Per Second
item.description: A comparison of video-generation billing between KIE.ai and reAPI, normalized at 720p, shows reAPI is cheaper on every Seedance tier and MiniMax H3, with savings from 8% to 25% (Seedance 2.0 drops from $0.205 to $0.154 per output second). The catch: reference-video requests bill input plus output seconds on both platforms, so a long reference clip can wipe out the saving. The author advises trimming the clip rather than picking a cheaper tier.

item.title: [infoq] 共识之外：Linux 生态系统中 AI 政策的碎片化现象
item.description: The article maps how Linux ecosystem projects are fragmenting on AI policy. GCC maintainers lean toward banning AI-generated patches over copyright and hallucination risks; the Linux kernel, led by Torvalds, requires maintainers to defend every line; Kubernetes mandates AI-use disclosure in PRs and forbids AI-written commit messages; Debian is weighing AI output against its Free Software Guidelines. The article is useful for teams deciding how to integrate AI assistance into code review.

item.title: [infoq] 谷歌发布 Angular v22，带来稳定的 Signal Forms、默认启用的 OnPush 以及实验性的 WebMCP
item.description: Angular v22 stabilizes Signal Forms, Angular Aria, and resource/rxResource/httpResource, makes OnPush the default change-detection strategy (the old default is renamed Eager), and adds @Service(), injectAsync lazy loading, and template spread/rest. It also ships experimental WebMCP to expose apps and forms to browser-based AI agents. Hacker News reviewers welcome the shift from RxJS-only form handling, but many still see the Angular compiler as a bottleneck for AI-assisted development.

item.title: [infoq] Stripe 利用 Graph Search 和状态机实现数据库修复自动化
item.description: Stripe's engineering team models its global MongoDB infrastructure as a graph and uses graph search combined with state machines to automate failure recovery. Replacing hardcoded repair sequences with Dijkstra-based pathfinding reduced database-related paging alerts by roughly 30%, saving about 200 pages and 12 days of shard anomalies per year. A useful pattern for teams managing complex distributed systems.

item.title: [hackernews] Anthropic's ‘watermark’ text adulteration in Claude is a perversion of writing
item.description: John Gruber of Daring Fireball criticizes Anthropic's plan to watermark all Claude outputs, including text, citing an EU regulation. Developers declare typed goals, actions, and conditions; a GOAP-inspired runtime planner assembles and re-plans action sequences. item.title: [hackernews] A Preview of DuckDB v2.0

The headline features include running DuckDB as a server, triggers, the VARIANT type, asynchronous I/O, a new SQL parser, and a new storage format. Developers using DuckDB for embedded analytics or planning server-side deployments should pay close attention.

item.title: [hackernews] How Bluesky draws its logo on screenshots
item.description: Developer Tim Marinin noticed that Bluesky screenshots show a logo in the corner even though the app UI doesn't display one — the spot is occupied by a Follow button. When he screenshotted during an app-switcher transition, the button was still visible, so he suspects Bluesky hooks the iOS screenshot shortcut and swaps in the logo at the last moment. He published his investigation.

item.title: [infoq] Valhalla 项目首次预览：JEP 401 重新定义 Java 对象的 == 运算符
item.description: JDK 28 now includes JEP 401 in preview: value classes declared with `value` have only final fields and no identity, and their == operator compares field values rather than references, while ordinary classes keep the old behavior. The preview is off by default and requires --enable-preview. It is significant for Java developers tracking JVM flattening and allocation-free layouts.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受

item.title: [infoq] Canva 分享了基于 S3 的架构，用于管理数亿个会话的会话撤销
item.description: Canva redesigned session revocation around immutable S3 objects holding compact 16-byte records, with an in-memory index pushed to application gateways, so most auth requests no longer hit the database. The shift cut revocation cache memory by 87.5%, lets workers process 2,000+ revocations per second, and speeds deployments. Teams operating very large session fleets can learn from this S3-as-orchestration design.

The article uses this lens to explain how to design better Skills. Useful for developers building AI skills.

item.title: [juejin] AI Harness 企业级落地实践（一）
item.description: This post explains AI Harness as applying engineering thinking to constrain AI agents with defined paradigms, aiming for more standardized and stable behavior. It lays out a five-stage workflow from project kickoff and requirements planning to review standards, implementation validation, and retrospective improvement. Useful for teams adopting enterprise-grade agent workflows, this is the first part of a practical series.
